question_text: A 61-year-old woman presents to her physician with foot tingling, numbness, and pain. She describes her pain as constant and burning and gives it 5 out of 10 on the visual analog pain scale. She also recalls several falls due to the numbness in her feet. She was diagnosed with diabetes mellitus and diabetic retinopathy 5 years ago. Since then, she takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily and had no follow-up visits to adjust her therapy. Her weight is 110 kg (242.5 lb), and her height is 176 cm (5 ft. 7 in). The vital signs are as follows: blood pressure is 150/90 mm Hg, heart rate is 72/min, respiratory rate is 12/min, and the temperature is 36.6°C (97.9°F). The patient has increased adiposity in the abdominal region with stretch marks. The respiratory examination is within normal limits. The cardiovascular exam is significant for a bilateral carotid bruit. The neurological examination shows bilateral decreased ankle reflex, symmetrically decreased touch sensation and absent vibration sensation in both feet up to the ankle. The gait is mildly ataxic. The Romberg test is positive with a tendency to fall to both sides, and significant worsening on eye closure. Which of the following medications should be used to manage the patient’s pain?
